description: Docker image that includes Wine and Winetricks for running Windows applications on Linux and macOS

summary.one_liner: A Docker image bundling Wine and Winetricks, run through a helper script to launch Windows applications on Linux and macOS with X11 forwarding, Xvfb, or an RDP desktop.
summary.what_it_does: The docker-wine script starts a container with Wine and Winetricks preinstalled, opening an interactive bash shell by default or running a given command such as wine notepad or winecfg. By default it forwards X11 to the host's X server and passes sound through PulseAudio. It can also run under an Xvfb virtual framebuffer, in attached no-tty mode, or as an XRDP server that a Remote Desktop client connects to, either as a foreground session or a detached daemon started and stopped with flags. The script supports running as root or as the current user's UID/GID and home path, and passes extra environment variables, devices and volumes through standard Docker syntax. A persistent volume named winehome keeps user data across container runs. The README also covers encrypting the RDP password with openssl, building the image locally with a build script, and using the image as a base for other Dockerfiles.
use_cases: run Windows programs on macOS with Wine
run Windows software on a headless server via remote desktop
persist Wine user data between container runs
build a custom Wine-based Docker image
how_to_run: wget <URL from README> && chmod +x docker-wine (Linux; README omits the URL)
curl -O <URL from README> && chmod +x docker-wine (macOS; README omits the URL)
./build (after cloning the repo, to build locally, then run with ./docker-wine --local)
notable: Switchable display modes: X11 forwarding, Xvfb virtual framebuffer, or XRDP remote desktop
Persistent winehome volume keeps user data when the container is removed or the image is updated
--as-me option maps the host user's UID, GID and home path into the container
caveats: The README says PulseAudio redirection on Linux and X11 on macOS need extra prerequisites that are not fully documented yet (a wiki is promised)
Remote RDP access requires TCP port 3389 to be open through the firewall
Passing --password exposes the password in the host process list, as the README notes
